abstract.text: This paper proposes a real-time approach for longterm inertial navigation based only on an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) for self-localizing wheeled robots. The approach builds upon two components: 1) a robust detector that uses recurrent deep neural networks to dynamically detect a variety of situations of interest, such as zero velocity or no lateral slip; and 2) a state-of-the-art Kalman filter which incorporates this knowledge as pseudo-measurements for localization. Evaluations on a publicly available car dataset demonstrates that the proposed scheme may achieve a final precision of 20 m for a 21 km long trajectory of a vehicle driving for over an hour, equipped with an IMU of moderate precision (the gyro drift rate is 10 deg/h). To our knowledge, this is the first paper which combines sophisticated deep learning techniques with state-ofthe-art filtering methods for pure inertial navigation on wheeled vehicles and as such opens up for novel data-driven inertial navigation techniques. Moreover, albeit taylored for IMU-only based localization, our method may be used as a component for self-localization of wheeled robots equipped with a more complete sensor suite.

identity.title: RINS-W: Robust Inertial Navigation System on Wheels

evidence.quote: The approach builds upon two components: 1) a robust detector that uses recurrent deep neural networks to dynamically detect a variety of situations of interest, such as zero velocity or no lateral slip

question.text: Can specific wheeled-vehicle motion profiles be detected in real time from raw IMU signals by recurrent deep neural networks and then used as pseudo-measurements in an invariant extended Kalman filter to enable accurate long-term IMU-only localization for wheeled robots?

relations.quote: We thus opt for an IEKF to perform the fusion between the IMU measurements and the detected specific motion profiles.
relations.why: The proposed fusion back-end is a Right Invariant Extended Kalman Filter, and the appendices follow its Jacobian derivations.

relations.quote: The IEKF [9] has already given rise to a commercial product in the field of high precision navigation, see [10,12].
relations.why: These works are cited as evidence that IEKF methods are mature enough for high-precision navigation and commercial use.

relations.quote: The following results are obtained on the complex urban LiDAR dataset [11]
relations.why: The paper evaluates RINS-W on the public Complex Urban LiDAR dataset, using its IMU data and ground truth.

relations.quote: Inertial navigation systems have long leveraged pseudo-measurements from IMU signals, e.g. the widespread Zero velocity UPdaTe (ZUPT) [19,20].
relations.why: RINS-W extends the classic zero-velocity pseudo-measurement idea to several detected wheeled-vehicle motion profiles.

relations.quote: Results are shown in Table 2 and demonstrate the detector is more accurate than this “ideal” AMVD.
relations.why: The learned detector is compared against an acceleration-moving variance detector and is reported to be more accurate.

relations.quote: Those methods are promising but difficult to transfer to a wheeled robots since they generally only consider horizontal planar motion
relations.why: The paper contrasts its wheeled-vehicle setting with prior deep-learning pedestrian inertial navigation, which often assumes planar motion.

relations.quote: The base core of the detector is a recurrent neural network, namely a Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) [8].
relations.why: The motion-profile detector is built from LSTM recurrent neural networks.

relations.quote: Note that our approach is different from more tightly coupled approaches such as [30].
relations.why: The proposed detector is separate from the filter, unlike more tightly coupled learned filtering approaches.

sections.summary: Introduces RINS-W as a pure-IMU inertial navigation method for wheeled robots, lists the paper's contributions, reviews related odometry/localization work, and gives the paper's structure.
sections.title: Introduction, Contributions, and Related Work

type.reason: The paper proposes a new method, derives its model and algorithm, and validates it experimentally on a public dataset.
